detailed_results.text: With 500 ha and $50,000 cash in Iowa, what is the shadow price of additional capital?
detailed_results.reply: With 500ha/50k cash capital is binding long before land. Peak cash need is second half Sep (f11) before soybean harvest. Max feasible ~175-176 ha soybean alone (0 corn) hits the 100k credit line (debt ~99.5k at f11). Corn is 778 USD/ha PV vs 663 USD/ha soybean but 1160 vs 839 USD/ha peak capital, so soybean gives higher NPV per USD of peak capital (0.78 vs 0.66). NPV at f0 ~164k ( ~114k farming profit +50k cash). Selling at harvest f12 (2026-10) is optimal: price gain 0.7-1.6 $/t/fortnight < storage 1.0 $/t/fortnight + interest. Shadow price: +1 USD own capital at f0 -> +~1.78 USD NPV discounted at 4% (= +0.78 net of depositing, about 0.75 USD per USD of extra credit line). The scarce stretch f2->f11 earns ~5.2% per fortnight ~ 250-300% annual, well above the 10% borrowing rate, until harvest repays debt.

detailed_results.text: How much does net present value change if capital is $100,000 instead of $50,000 on 500 ha in Iowa?

Sell soybean at harvest f12 (2026-10) - storing is break-even at deposit rate (4%) and loss at credit rate (10%), corn storing is loss. NPV ~USD 253-255k. With USD 50k optimal is ~175-176 ha soybean, NPV ~USD 164k. So NPV is ~USD 89-90k higher (+USD 50k is the extra capital, ~USD 39-40k is extra economic profit, ~0.79 per extra dollar above deposit). Corn is more profitable per ha (USD 778 vs 663 PV) but less profitable per USD of scarce early cash (0.67 vs 0.79), so soybean dominates when capital is scarce. Rotation 50% (250 ha) not binding.
